The defcon board — by gameweek

Defenders and midfielders only, ranked each gameweek on shots, penalty-adjusted expected goals, expected assists and defensive contributions — and on the four together.

Covering GW1, GW2, GW3, GW4, GW5 · 347 defenders and midfielders · shots and penalties from fbref, everything else from the FPL API. Every penalty attempt costs its taker 0.75 xG in the week he took it. Shots, xG and xA board → Pre-season board → In-season app →

Read this first

Where the numbers come from. No single source has all of them. fbref publishes shots and penalties attempted, one sheet per gameweek, each one cumulative to the end of that gameweek — so a single gameweek is the sheet minus its predecessor. The FPL API publishes expected goals, expected assists, defensive contributions and minutes, already week by week. The two are joined player by player; the join is audited at the foot of the page.

Penalties. A penalty is worth about 0.79 xG in the models, and it tells you who takes penalties rather than who is getting shots away. Left in, one spot kick outranks four good chances. So each attempt fbref records costs its taker 0.75 xG in that gameweek, and the ranking uses what is left. The weeks it applied are listed below, and marked with a small red p in the tables.

How the ranking works. Within a gameweek, over the defenders and midfielders who actually played, each of shots, penalty-adjusted xG, xA and defensive contributions is ranked with 1 the best; ties share the mean rank, so nobody gains by sitting in a crowd of zeros. The four ranks are added and the sum re-ranked from 1 — that number is the cell on the Aggregate ranking tab. The other four tabs show the raw number with its own rank in that category in brackets beside it, which is the rank that belongs with a shots count — the aggregate is mostly about the other categories, and has its own tab. Hover any cell for all of it: the four category ranks, the raw numbers, and what they summed to.

A player who did not play is blank (—), not zero and not last: he was injured, rested, suspended or an unused substitute, and the data does not say which. But a column of blanks cannot be summed honestly, because missing a gameweek would then improve a player's total. So Total charges a missed gameweek that week's last place, and Avg is the mean over the gameweeks he actually played. They answer different questions — Total asks who has been most useful so far, Avg asks who is best when he plays — and GWs sits between them so you can always see which is which. Sorting is on any column; blanks always sink.

Totals, not rates. A substitute who plays ten minutes is ranked against a man who played ninety, on the same raw numbers. That is the honest way to answer "who did most this gameweek", but it is not "who is best per minute" — a cameo with one shot in it will outrank a quiet full ninety. Mins is on every row so you can see which you are looking at.

What the bottom of the table means. GW1 7 (3%); GW2 14 (5%); GW3 14 (6%); GW4 10 (4%); GW5 9 (4%) of the players who played registered nothing at all in any of the four categories. They are genuinely tied, they all share the same rank, and no ordering among them means anything. The field each week: GW1 255; GW2 259; GW3 250; GW4 252; GW5 246.

Adding a gameweek. Drop a new GW<n> sheet into data/2026-27/fbref_shots.xlsx — cumulative, like the others — re-run scraper_fpl.py for the FPL side, then python build_shots.py. The sheet names are the gameweek numbers; the workbook's own Week column is a row rank and is ignored.

top 10 that gameweek   top 30   — no minutes   p penalty charged that week   ✓ cleared the 2-point defensive bar that week

On the Shots, xG (pen-adjusted), xA and Defensive contributions tabs a cell reads value (rank) — the rank is that player's place in that category that gameweek, not the aggregate, because the aggregate is mostly about the other categories. It shares the mean where players tie, so (82.5) is a tie spanning 82nd and 83rd. The shading follows that same rank, and the columns still sort on the value.

Defensive contributions, and the 2 points

What is counted. FPL's own tally of qualifying defensive actions. For a defender that is clearances, blocks, interceptions and tackles; for a midfielder it adds recoveries. The board ranks that raw count — it is what "defensive contributions" means, and it is the same treatment the other three categories get.

The 2 points are a different question. FPL pays them at a threshold, and the threshold is not the same for both: Defenders 10; Midfielders 12. A midfielder's count includes recoveries and needs two more of them, so the raw count and the reward do not line up. Rather than distort the ranking to patch that, the threshold is shown directly: a cell that cleared it carries a green ✓, and the DC pts column counts the gameweeks a player has done it. So far: defenders 107 of 533 (20%); midfielders 56 of 729 (8%) of player-gameweeks.

Three of the four categories are attacking, so the aggregate leans that way and midfielders fill the head of the table. Use the position filter to read it as a defenders' board, or sort on the Defensive contributions tab — which opens on the season total — to read it as a pure defensive one.

How the two sources were joined

fbref writes display names (Bruno Fernandes); FPL writes first_second lowercased (bruno_borges fernandes). Names are normalised and assigned one-to-one, best match first. A club agreeing helps but is not required — FPL reports a player's current club, so a deadline-day move disagrees with the club he actually played for. Whatever is left over is settled on minutes, which is what catches the nicknames no string match will: fbref's Beto is FPL's norberto bercique gomes betuncal, its Costinha is joão pedro loureiro da costa.

Minutes then audit every pair. Two sources that counted the same man's minutes independently are the check on whether the join is right, and anything they disagree on by more than 10 minutes is named here rather than quietly shipped. So is anyone FPL says was on the pitch that fbref does not list, because he would otherwise be ranked as having taken no shot when the truth is that nobody counted them.

Every match the names alone did not settle (63 of 421)

name inside name — one name is a subset of the other, so Bruno Fernandes is Bruno Borges Fernandes. surname only — the surnames agree and the first names do not, accepted at the same club. one token shared — a single name in common, the weakest string match, so read these rows. minutes played — the names share nothing at all and the match rests entirely on both sources having counted the same minutes at the same club, with exactly one candidate close enough. Every row is shown with both minute counts so you can check it yourself.

Players who have changed club (5)

Not an error, and it shows up in two ways. A player who moved during the gameweeks covered has two fbref rows, one per spell — the season is split by club — and they are summed back together before anything else happens, because the shots belong to the man, not the shirt. A player who moved after the last gameweek shown is still at his old club in fbref and already at his new one in FPL. The two minute counts are the check on both: they are of the whole man either way, and they agree.
